On Fri, Apr 30, 2021 at 12:32 PM Satish Menon <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Dear Madhu and Rajat,
Was so great catching up with you over the call.
As we discussed, I am sharing a synopsis of a few COVID-specific programs addressing health and economic
recovery that USAID/India is focusing on.
1) Health Blended Financing Facility: USAID/India in collaboration with several government organizations and
foundations has established a Health blended financing initiative to support the immediate deployment high-impact
solutions such as oxygen delivery systems, cold chain storage solutions for vaccines, low-cost RT-PCR kits, artificial
intelligence for tracing COVID-19 hotspots, precision surveillance diagnostic systems and community- based
interventions to address the second wave of COVID-19 pandemic.
2) REVIVE -Blended Finance Facility supporting livelihoods of informal workers impacted by COVID: The
REVIVE Alliance is supporting the informal sector whose livelihoods are impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic, with a
focus on women and youth. The REVIVE Alliance facilitates skills development, technical assistance, vocational
skills, business training, and market linkages to complement the financial support. Launched in October 2020 by
Samhita-Collective Good Foundation and supported by USAID, Omidyar Network India, Michael & Susan Dell
Foundation, British High Commission, the United Nations Development Programme India. The REVIVE Alliance has
also partnered with the Government of India's National Skills Development Corporation program. The Alliance
engages experts from J-PAL South Asia, Georgetown University and the Atlantic Council for a robust monitoring and
evaluations to understand the impact of this blended-finance facility, the largest of its kind to be tested in India.
3) Communications on COVID appropriate behaviors: USAID has been working with UNICEF to support the
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in the development of a comprehensive Communications Strategy
complemented by an array of materials and guides, as well as community mobilization and social media activities
promoting Covid Appropriate Behaviours(CAB) and COVID related stigma and discrimination.
Further, as you mentioned regarding the proposed intervention around health communications, we are open to
exploring the same with WHO.
Shall we set up a follow-up call next week to chat about the concrete next steps?
Best wishes, good health & safety to all,
Satish
Best,
